structures.name: Section Warden service house
structures.structure: Wet-oak post-and-beam frame on mismatched drowned-limestone blocks and driven piles, with replaceable reed lattice bracing and a visibly maintained pile-collar route below.
exterior: low reed roof tied with sacrificial flood-release cords
pitch-cloth storm skirt stopping above the ordinary flood mark
new pale wicker repairs against older blackened oak
raised rain cistern and crooked guide-lantern hook visible from the causeway
two materially distinct exits: dry causeway step and low rescue boat hatch
weathering: pile settlement creates a legible lean without collapsing door clearances
algae and lamp-oil rainbow record a continuous historic waterline
handled thresholds polish while windward reed faces gray and split
fresh wicker stays pale enough to show which family route is maintained

sensory.acoustic: Each plank gives a different hollow note above blackwater.
sensory.scent: Rain-dark oak, lamp oil, and cold peat.

sensory.acoustic: Drips strike differently marked basins instead of an ambient water loop.

sensory.scent: Mudfish broth, peat smoke, damp wool, and bronze valve grease.

sensory.visual: The whole household fits around a visibly gauged cistern without blocking the ladder landing.
sensory.acoustic: Rain enters the tank as a slow measured resonance, not a waterfall roar.
sensory.scent: Clean rain, reed resin, and cool clay.

sensory.visual: A red-banded rescue latch stays unobstructed above a narrow service skiff berth.
sensory.acoustic: Hull taps, collar creak, and water slap disclose movement below the occupied floor.
sensory.scent: Tar, blackwater, bronze, and sealed reed cage.

sensory.acoustic: Reed knives rasp while crosswind clicks drying stems against the rail.
sensory.scent: Cut reed, drying peat, wet slate, and lamp oil.

structures.name: Four-bank visibility exchange
structures.structure: Four independently braced stilt banks, two paired Escrow frames, a finite living-borrower ledger, a ferry edge, and one raised clear-air refuge joined by narrow accountable causeways.
exterior: four bank silhouettes remain individually readable through ground fog
paired frames are low horizontal structures and never resemble four separate creatures
guide lanterns mark ordinary paths while the exchange boundary uses unlit rope and clear-air movement
the raised refuge is visibly above and outside the exchange envelope
dry and boat egress depart in different directions with no shared first segment
weathering: each bank carries a different settlement lean and repair history
waterline algae and pile collars disclose seasonal rise
fog-wet surfaces are dark except where hands polish ledger rails
the seasonal dark bank carries newer high rope and red-banded fire fittings

sensory.visual: One numbered-by-form socket, never text, sits beside an ordinary public causeway rail.
sensory.acoustic: The socket answers with one low timber note only when the other three banks are loaded.
sensory.scent: Wet oak, cold limestone, and ferry pitch.

rooms.name: Bank B ferry and delivery deck

sensory.visual: A load-marked ferry cradle and separate rescue berth prevent delivery, quest exchange, and egress from reading as one dock.
sensory.acoustic: Winch brake, hollow fender knocks, and recalled-boat bells separate operating states.
sensory.scent: Tar, mudfish water, lamp-oil crates, and wet rope.

sensory.visual: Two distant paired frames terminate at one physically finite ledger station; no reflection is given a ledger position.
sensory.acoustic: One task-light relay clicks after two frame tensions agree, followed by spoken living counts.
sensory.scent: Lamp oil, wet bronze, reed paper, and clean rain duct air.

rooms.name: Bank C household and exchange-edge deck

sensory.visual: Household screens stop before the marked edge so privacy never hides the exchange boundary.
sensory.acoustic: Clear-air reeds hiss against a sudden absence of ordinary fog-muted sound.
sensory.scent: Rain, family cooking smoke, clean reed air, and blackwater.

rooms.name: Bank D and seasonal dark watch

sensory.visual: The fourth socket, high return rope, and deliberately hooded lantern make ordinary, failure, and fire states distinct.
sensory.acoustic: Reed crosswind and a single warning clapper replace market noise here.
sensory.scent: Wet char, cold rope, peat dust, and emergency canvas.

sensory.visual: Dry pale boards and an uninterrupted view of all four banks prove the refuge is outside the dark exchange volume.
sensory.acoustic: Clear-air duct breath remains audible when fog erases sounds below.
sensory.scent: Clean rain, dry reed, potable water, and no lamp smoke.

egress.independenceRule: The two paths share only the refuge anchor; they use exact distinct interior vertices, exact directed forward and return edges, distinct failure domains, 2.2 meter minimum clear spans, and different protected destinations.

utilities.failureState: Isolate at the service and refuge ports, log demand, and leave both egress domains physically open.
Brake and isolate the winch; publish a physical recall state without closing boat egress.

Isolate the named duct only; the refuge remains a dry muster space and the exchange closes before air is borrowed from occupants.
Isolate a damaged branch while retaining bucket, canvas, and alternate-bank hose reach.
Seal the reed cage above flood, stop collection before fog fall, and keep it outside clean-water and ledger-light paths.

routes.accessibility: The occupied level and balcony use clear 1.2 m thresholds; loft and water-hatch vertical segments are specialist/refuge links and do not substitute for external step-free egress.
The route is a directed join-and-split network, never a linear bank corridor; distinct intra-room ports preserve Frame AB, ledger, and Frame CD topology.
Bank A, ferry, and delivery are three distinct ports; recall state ends supply runs but does not erase protected boat egress.
The physical ferry-causeway-Bank C path stays maintenance-traversable in every phase; the Loaner exchange is staffed only during fog fall, and both protected egress domains remain separate.
Two distinct bank returns reach the refuge without using either protected egress interior vertex.
Source segments preserve the service-maintenance-causeway chain and separate seasonal-watch span; local house segments expose utility and fire-watch rooms.
The detailed refuge-domain-destination path retains 2.2 meter clear width, while direct refuge and service returns remain distinct accepted edges.

exteriorRead: Compose Warden Reed as a long inhabited causeway settlement, not a swamp village scattered at random: repeated stilt rhythms break only at family-owned sections, ferry cuts, and the four-bank exchange.
Keep human domestic scale in the foreground—bowls, wicker repair, fish cages, laundry, tool racks—while fog and the Escrow create ominous depth without turning every surface into horror ornament.
From any quest approach, show all four distinct bank silhouettes, one low spanning body, and one visibly higher dry refuge in the same navigable composition.
Let waterline, settlement lean, pale new wicker, ownership cuts, guide-lantern count, and high rope carry state; never use floating labels or glowing UI runes.
Preserve blackwater reflections as visually persuasive but physically unserviced: reflected doors, people, and lights receive no latch, socket, ledger rail, or collision volume.
interiorRead: The service house is crowded, warm, patched, and operational; it must feel inhabited before it feels quest-relevant.
Separate wet/dirty, dry domestic, clean water, fire-watch, and rescue-hatch zones through floor texture, storage discipline, smell, and sound rather than color-coded game rooms.
The ledger gallery is a sparse working station with reachable mechanisms, visible maintenance access, and exactly one finite counting position for each living borrower.
The raised refuge uses pale dry material, clear-air movement, drinking water, and two unmistakable departures; no exchange shadow enters its envelope.
Every threshold exposes its current state through hinges, ropes, latches, rails, shutters, or physical absence; decorative closed doors are forbidden.
light: Baseline is moonless teal-gray ambient light with cold rain sheen and strong occlusion by reed walls and ground fog.
Warm practicals are sparse crooked guide lanterns, hooded ledger task light, peat-stove glow, and red-banded fire cabinet reflections.
The refuge reads by cold clear raking light and dry pale bounce, not holy glow; the exchange reads by silhouette and moving clear air, not magical particles.
At first light, reveal repair evidence and living-count positions before widening visibility across the mire.
weather: Steady rain, ground fog, still-water condensation, and low wind dominate; crosswind appears only at causeway gaps and the work balcony.
Seasonal blackwater may rise one meter in the candidate design storm, but ordinary thresholds, rescue hatches, and refuge relation remain legible.
Fog-fall is a volumetric boundary event with finite extent at the marked edge; it is not a global post-process covering safe cells.
Late cold can lock shallow channels, shifting deliveries to the dry causeway while preserving manual rescue craft at the deeper ferry return.
